classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish perpendicular height from slant height, halve given diameters, and link the prompted Pythagoras calculation to the cone surface-area formula.

content.prompt: Calculate the surface area of these solids. You will need to find the slant height. Round your answer to 1 decimal place.

spec.description: Upright cone with hidden rear rim, perpendicular height, base diameter and right-angle marker. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular height 28 cm; base diameter 25 cm. The 28 cm measurement belongs to the axis, not the sloping silhouette.

spec.description: Horizontal cone with its visible circular base on the left and apex on the right; the entire base rim is visible. Radius and perpendicular axis are dashed and meet at a right angle.
spec.mathematics: Radius 0.3 m and perpendicular height 1.8 m.

spec.description: Tilted cone with apex upper-left, an oblique visible base rim, dashed base diameter and dashed perpendicular height. The height and diameter meet at the base centre with a right-angle marker.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular height 9 cm; base diameter 18 cm, hence radius 9 cm.
